name: Hydrogen
description: Lightest element and the most abundant chemical substance in the universe. Essential component of water and all organic compounds.

name: Helium
description: Second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe. Colorless, odorless, inert monatomic gas.

name: Lithium
description: Lightest metal and lightest solid element. Widely used in rechargeable batteries and psychiatric medication.

name: Beryllium
description: Steel-gray, strong, lightweight alkaline earth metal. Used in aerospace materials, X-ray windows, and particle physics.

name: Boron
description: Metalloid essential for plant growth. Used in borosilicate glass, detergents, and as a semiconductor dopant.

name: Carbon
description: Basis of all known life on Earth. Forms more compounds than any other element, from diamonds to organic molecules.

name: Nitrogen
description: Makes up 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Essential for amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids in all living organisms.

name: Oxygen
description: Most abundant element in Earth's crust. Essential for respiration and combustion. Forms water with hydrogen.

name: Fluorine
description: Most electronegative and reactive of all elements. Used in toothpaste, Teflon, and refrigerants.

name: Neon
description: Gives a distinct reddish-orange glow in vacuum discharge tubes. Used in neon signs and high-voltage indicators.

name: Sodium
description: Soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal. Essential for nerve function. Common as sodium chloride (table salt).

name: Magnesium
description: Lightweight structural metal used in alloys. Essential for chlorophyll in plants and hundreds of enzymes in humans.

name: Aluminum
description: Most abundant metal in Earth's crust. Lightweight, corrosion-resistant. Used in packaging, transportation, and construction.

name: Silicon
description: Second most abundant element in Earth's crust. Fundamental to semiconductor technology and modern electronics.

name: Phosphorus
description: Essential for life — found in DNA, RNA, and ATP. Used in fertilizers, detergents, and matches.

name: Sulfur
description: Bright yellow crystalline solid. Essential for proteins and enzymes. Used in sulfuric acid production and vulcanization.

name: Chlorine
description: Yellow-green gas with a pungent odor. Essential for water purification, disinfectants, and PVC production.

name: Argon
description: Third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere. Used in welding, lighting, and as a protective atmosphere for growing crystals.

name: Potassium
description: Essential nutrient for all living cells. Highly reactive silvery-white metal. Used in fertilizers and potassium hydroxide.

name: Calcium
description: Most abundant metal in the human body. Essential for bones, teeth, and cellular signaling. Found in limestone and chalk.

name: Scandium
description: Silvery-white metallic element. Used in aerospace alloys and high-intensity metal halide lamps.

name: Titanium
description: Strong, lustrous, corrosion-resistant transition metal. Used in aerospace, medical implants, and sporting goods.

name: Vanadium
description: Hard, silvery-grey metal. Used to strengthen steel alloys. Found in some minerals and fossil fuel deposits.

name: Chromium
description: Hard, lustrous metal with a high melting point. Used in stainless steel, chrome plating, and pigments.

name: Manganese
description: Essential trace element for all living organisms. Used in steel production and dry cell batteries.

name: Iron
description: Most common element on Earth by mass. Foundation of steel industry. Essential for hemoglobin in blood.

name: Cobalt
description: Hard, lustrous, silver-gray metal. Used in lithium-ion batteries, superalloys, and blue pigments.

name: Nickel
description: Silvery-white lustrous metal with a slight golden tinge. Used in stainless steel, coins, and batteries.

name: Copper
description: Highly ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity. Essential for modern infrastructure.

name: Zinc
description: Bluish-white, lustrous metal. Essential trace element for humans. Used in galvanizing steel and in batteries.

name: Gallium
description: Soft, silvery metal that melts near room temperature. Used in semiconductors, LEDs, and solar panels.

name: Germanium
description: Lustrous, hard-brittle metalloid. Important semiconductor material used in fiber optics and infrared optics.

name: Arsenic
description: Metalloid known for its toxicity. Used in semiconductors, pesticides, and wood preservatives.

name: Selenium
description: Essential trace element with antioxidant properties. Used in glass-making, pigments, and photovoltaic cells.

name: Bromine
description: Reddish-brown liquid at room temperature, one of only two liquid elements. Used in flame retardants and pharmaceuticals.

name: Krypton
description: Colorless, odorless noble gas. Used in fluorescent lamps, flash photography, and as an insulating gas.

name: Rubidium
description: Soft, silvery-white alkali metal. Highly reactive. Used in atomic clocks and specialized glass.

name: Strontium
description: Silvery-yellow alkaline earth metal. Used in fireworks for red color, ferrite magnets, and toothpaste.

name: Yttrium
description: Silvery-metallic transition metal. Used in LEDs, lasers, superconductors, and cancer treatment drugs.

name: Zirconium
description: Lustrous, grey-white metal. Highly resistant to corrosion. Used in nuclear reactors and ceramic materials.

name: Niobium
description: Light grey, crystalline metal. Used in superconducting magnets, aerospace alloys, and hypoallergenic jewelry.

name: Molybdenum
description: Silvery metal with very high melting point. Essential trace element. Used in high-strength steel alloys.

name: Technetium
description: Lightest element with no stable isotopes. First artificially produced element. Used in nuclear medicine imaging.

name: Ruthenium
description: Rare transition metal of the platinum group. Used in electronics, solar cells, and catalytic chemistry.

name: Rhodium
description: Ultra-rare, silvery-white noble metal. Most expensive precious metal. Used in catalytic converters and jewelry.

name: Palladium
description: Rare silvery-white metal. Key component in catalytic converters, electronics, and hydrogen purification.

name: Silver
description: Highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any element. Used in jewelry, photography, and electronics.

name: Cadmium
description: Soft, bluish-white metal. Used in NiCd batteries, pigments, and as a neutron absorber in nuclear reactors.

name: Indium
description: Soft, malleable metal with a brilliant lustre. Used in touchscreens (ITO), semiconductors, and low-melting alloys.

name: Tin
description: Silvery, malleable metal that resists corrosion. Used in tin plating, solder, and bronze alloys since antiquity.

name: Antimony
description: Lustrous gray metalloid. Used in flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, and semiconductor devices.

name: Tellurium
description: Brittle, mildly toxic metalloid. Used in solar panels (CdTe), thermoelectric devices, and as an alloy additive.

name: Iodine
description: Lustrous purple-black nonmetal. Essential for thyroid hormones. Used in medicine, photography, and dyes.

name: Xenon
description: Dense noble gas found in trace amounts in atmosphere. Used in flash lamps, arc lamps, and ion propulsion.

name: Cesium
description: Soft, silvery-gold alkali metal with lowest melting point of any metal. Defines the SI second in atomic clocks.

name: Barium
description: Soft, silvery alkaline earth metal. Used in drilling fluids, barium meals for X-ray imaging, and fireworks.

name: Lanthanum
description: Soft, ductile, silvery-white metal. Head of the lanthanide series. Used in camera lenses and catalytic converters.

name: Cerium
description: Most abundant rare earth element. Used in catalytic converters, self-cleaning ovens, and glass polishing.

name: Praseodymium
description: Soft, silvery, malleable rare earth metal. Used in strong permanent magnets and aircraft engines.

name: Neodymium
description: Used to make the strongest permanent magnets known (NdFeB). Essential for electric motors and headphones.

name: Promethium
description: Only lanthanide with no stable isotopes. Extremely rare. Used in nuclear batteries and luminous paint.

name: Samarium
description: Moderately hard silvery metal. Used in samarium-cobalt magnets, nuclear reactor control rods, and cancer treatment.

name: Europium
description: Most reactive rare earth element. Used in red and blue phosphors for displays and Euro banknote security features.

name: Gadolinium
description: Silvery-white metal with unique magnetic properties. Used as MRI contrast agent and in nuclear reactor shielding.

name: Terbium
description: Silvery-white rare earth metal. Used in green phosphors for displays, solid-state devices, and fuel cells.

name: Dysprosium
description: Relatively soft silvery metal. Used in neodymium magnets to improve high-temperature performance and in nuclear reactors.

name: Holmium
description: Has the highest magnetic moment of any naturally occurring element. Used in nuclear control rods and solid-state lasers.

name: Erbium
description: Silvery-white solid metal. Used in fiber optic amplifiers, lasers, and as a pink colorant for glass and ceramics.

name: Thulium
description: Least abundant lanthanide in the Earth's crust. Used in portable X-ray devices and high-temperature superconductors.

name: Ytterbium
description: Soft, malleable rare earth element. Used in stress gauges, lasers, and as a metallurgical additive.

name: Lutetium
description: Hardest and densest lanthanide. Used in PET scan detectors, refining petroleum, and LED phosphors.

name: Hafnium
description: Lustrous, silvery metal resistant to corrosion. Used in nuclear control rods, plasma torches, and microprocessors.

name: Tantalum
description: Hard, blue-gray, lustrous metal. Highly corrosion-resistant. Used in capacitors, medical implants, and jet engines.

name: Tungsten
description: Has the highest melting point of all elements. Used in light bulb filaments, cutting tools, and military applications.

name: Rhenium
description: One of the rarest elements in Earth's crust. Has third highest melting point. Used in jet engine superalloys.

name: Osmium
description: Densest naturally occurring element. Hard, brittle, bluish-white metal. Used in fountain pen nibs and electrical contacts.

name: Iridium
description: Most corrosion-resistant metal known. Second-densest element. Used in spark plugs, crucibles, and the standard kilogram.

name: Platinum
description: Dense, malleable, precious metal. Used in catalytic converters, jewelry, and chemotherapy drugs.

name: Gold
description: Bright, slightly reddish-yellow precious metal. Highly valued throughout history. Used in jewelry, electronics, and currency.

name: Mercury
description: Only metal liquid at standard conditions. Used in thermometers, barometers, and fluorescent lighting.

name: Thallium
description: Soft, gray metal that tarnishes in air. Highly toxic. Used in electronics, optics, and nuclear medicine.

name: Lead
description: Dense, soft, malleable metal. Known since antiquity. Used in batteries, radiation shielding, and construction.

name: Bismuth
description: Crystalline, brittle metal with a pink tinge. Least toxic heavy metal. Used in medicines and cosmetics.

name: Polonium
description: Extremely rare and highly radioactive. Discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie. Used in anti-static devices.

name: Astatine
description: Rarest naturally occurring element on Earth. Highly radioactive. Studied for use in targeted cancer treatment.

name: Radon
description: Radioactive noble gas formed from radium decay. Colorless and odorless. Second leading cause of lung cancer.

name: Francium
description: Second rarest naturally occurring element. Most unstable of the first 101 elements. Extremely radioactive.

name: Radium
description: Intensely radioactive, glowing faintly blue. Discovered by Marie Curie. Historically used in luminous paints.

name: Actinium
description: Head of the actinide series. Intensely radioactive, glowing blue in the dark. Used in neutron sources.

name: Thorium
description: Weakly radioactive metal. Potential nuclear fuel alternative to uranium. Used in gas mantles and TIG welding.

name: Protactinium
description: Dense, silvery-gray, radioactive metal. Extremely rare. Has no practical applications outside scientific research.

name: Uranium
description: Dense, silvery-white radioactive metal. Primary fuel for nuclear power plants and nuclear weapons.

name: Neptunium
description: First transuranic element. Silvery, radioactive metal. Used in neutron detection instruments.

name: Plutonium
description: Radioactive actinide metal with silvery appearance. Used in nuclear weapons, power sources for spacecraft.

name: Americium
description: Synthetic radioactive element. Most common use is in household smoke detectors as an ionizing source.

name: Curium
description: Named after Marie and Pierre Curie. Hard, dense, silvery metal. Used as alpha particle source in space exploration.

name: Berkelium
description: Named after Berkeley, California. Radioactive element produced in nuclear reactors. Used in scientific research.

name: Californium
description: Powerful neutron emitter. Used in nuclear reactor startup, metal detection, and treatment of certain cancers.

name: Einsteinium
description: Named after Albert Einstein. Discovered in debris of first hydrogen bomb test. No practical applications yet.

name: Fermium
description: Named after Enrico Fermi. Synthetic element discovered in H-bomb debris. No uses outside scientific research.

name: Mendelevium
description: Named after Dmitri Mendeleev. Produced in tiny amounts by particle bombardment. Used only in research.

name: Nobelium
description: Named after Alfred Nobel. Synthetic radioactive element. Only produced in particle accelerators for research.

name: Lawrencium
description: Final member of the actinide series. Named after Ernest Lawrence. Only produced in particle accelerators.

name: Rutherfordium
description: First transactinide element. Named after Ernest Rutherford. Highly radioactive with very short half-life.

name: Dubnium
description: Named after Dubna, Russia. Synthetic superheavy element. Only a few atoms have ever been produced.

name: Seaborgium
description: Named after Glenn T. Seaborg. Synthetic element created by nuclear bombardment. Extremely unstable.

name: Bohrium
description: Named after Niels Bohr. Synthetic superheavy element with extremely short half-life. No practical uses.

name: Hassium
description: Named after the German state of Hesse. Synthetic element with extremely short half-life. Used only in research.

name: Meitnerium
description: Named after physicist Lise Meitner. Extremely radioactive synthetic element with no practical applications.

name: Darmstadtium
description: Named after Darmstadt, Germany. Superheavy element with extremely short half-life on the order of microseconds.

name: Roentgenium
description: Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays. Synthetic element with extremely short half-life.

name: Copernicium
description: Named after astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus. Predicted to be a volatile liquid metal at room temperature.

name: Nihonium
description: Named after Japan (Nihon). First element discovered in an Asian country. Extremely unstable synthetic element.

name: Flerovium
description: Named after Flerov Laboratory. Superheavy element predicted to be volatile. Near proposed island of stability.

name: Moscovium
description: Named after Moscow Oblast. Synthetic superheavy element. Only a few atoms have ever been observed.

name: Livermorium
description: Named after Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. Extremely radioactive with half-life of milliseconds.

name: Tennessine
description: Named after Tennessee, USA. Second heaviest known element. Predicted to have some halogen-like properties.

name: Oganesson
description: Heaviest known element. Named after Yuri Oganessian. Predicted to be a solid noble gas. Extremely unstable.
